clinical_context: HIV antiretroviral (now largely replaced by newer agents)
system_prompt: You are an expert computational medicinal chemist. Always respond with valid JSON containing a 'modifications' list. Each modification must include 'description', 'smiles', and 'rationale' fields.

modifications.description: Introduce a fluorine atom on the aromatic ring to enhance binding interactions with the protease active site via halogen bonding.
modifications.rationale: Fluorine substitution can improve binding potency by forming halogen bonds with residues in the HIV-1 protease active site, increasing specificity and affinity.

modifications.description: Replace a phenyl group with a 4-pyridyl group to introduce additional hydrogen bonding capability.
modifications.rationale: Switching a phenyl group to a 4-pyridyl group can enable additional hydrogen bonding interactions with the protease active site, potentially enhancing selectivity and binding strength.

modifications.description: Add a hydroxymethyl group to the benzylic position to increase hydrogen bonding interactions.
modifications.rationale: Introducing a hydroxymethyl group can promote additional hydrogen bonds with residues in the HIV-1 protease active site, improving binding potency and selectivity.

modifications.description: Incorporate a cyclopropyl group in place of one phenyl ring to reduce molecular flexibility and improve binding affinity.
modifications.rationale: Replacing a phenyl ring with a cyclopropyl group reduces flexibility, enhancing binding affinity by favoring a conformation that complements the protease active site.

modifications.description: Add a methyl group to the secondary amide nitrogen to improve hydrophobic interactions with the protease.
modifications.rationale: Methylation of the amide nitrogen can enhance hydrophobic contacts in the active site, increasing binding potency without significantly altering the molecule's polarity.
